actions: Apply agricultural lime (calcium carbonate) or dolomite broadcast and thoroughly incorporate into the top 15 cm before planting.
Incorporate well-decomposed farmyard manure (FYM) or compost to buffer soil acidity and enhance phosphorus availability.
Band apply phosphorus fertilizers (rock phosphate or SSP) rather than broadcasting to reduce soil P fixation.
Select acid-tolerant crop varieties and consider tea, pineapple, or pulses where acidity is persistent.
note: Confirm with a local soil test and an agronomist before applying amendments. Never apply unmeasured lime doses.

actions: Apply agricultural gypsum (calcium sulphate) or elemental sulphur to displace exchangeable sodium and lower rhizosphere pH.
Incorporate green manuring crops (such as Dhaincha / Sesbania aculeata) during pre-monsoon showers.
Use acidifying nitrogenous fertilizers like ammonium sulphate in place of urea.
Apply zinc sulphate and iron chelates foliar or soil-banded as micronutrient availability is restricted at high pH.
note: Confirm with a local soil test and an agronomist before applying amendments.

actions: Apply mined gypsum based on gypsum requirement (GR) test to replace adsorbed sodium ions with calcium.
Provide adequate leaching with non-saline irrigation water and ensure functional field drainage outlets.
Incorporate deep green manures (Dhaincha) and ensure continuous vegetative cover to prevent sodium crusting.
Adopt sodicity-tolerant crops such as barley, karnal grass, or salt-tolerant rice varieties (e.g. CSR-36, CSR-43).
note: Confirm with a local soil test and an agronomist before applying amendments.

actions: Leach soluble salts below root zone by ponding fresh irrigation water and maintaining sub-surface drainage.
Construct field bunds to harvest monsoon rainwater for in-situ salt washing and flushing.
Adopt salt-tolerant crops like barley, cotton, sugarbeet, mustard, and sorghum.
Use drip irrigation with frequent light irrigations to keep salts pushed to the wetting perimeter.
note: Confirm with a local soil test and an agronomist before applying amendments.

actions: Apply 10-15 tonnes/ha of well-rotted farmyard manure (FYM), compost, or vermicompost prior to seedbed preparation.
Practice green manuring by incorporating Sesbania (Dhaincha) or Sunnhemp (Crotalaria juncea) at 45-50 days growth.
Adopt conservation agriculture: retain 30% or more crop residues on the surface and avoid stubble burning.
Include leguminous cover crops in crop rotation cycles to restore soil carbon and biological activity.
note: Confirm with a local soil test and an agronomist before applying amendments.

issue: Coarse sandy texture with low water and nutrient retention
actions: Incorporate bulky organic manures, pressmud, or biochar to build up soil structure and water-holding capacity.
Apply organic mulches (straw, dry leaves) to suppress surface soil evaporation and lower soil temperature.
Install drip irrigation with fertigation to supply nutrients in small, frequent split doses and prevent leaching losses.
Choose drought-hardy and tap-rooted crops such as pearl millet, castor, groundnut, and cluster bean.
note: Confirm with a local soil test and an agronomist before applying amendments.

issue: Heavy clay with poor internal drainage or compaction
actions: Construct broad bed and furrow (BBF) systems or raised beds to prevent root-zone waterlogging during intense rains.
Provide field periphery surface drainage channels to evacuate excess runoff quickly.
Avoid tillage operations when soil is too wet to prevent severe subsoil compaction and hardpan development.
Apply gypsum or organic amendments to promote flocculation and enhance water infiltration.
note: Confirm with a local soil test and an agronomist before applying amendments.

issue: Low moisture score or severe root-zone water deficit
actions: Deploy micro-irrigation systems (drip or micro-sprinklers) saving 30-50% water compared to flood irrigation.
Construct farm ponds (khet talab) or check dams for on-farm rainwater harvesting and life-saving irrigation.
Adopt residue mulching (paddy straw, sugarcane trash) to reduce soil moisture evaporation by up to 35%.
Switch to low-water-demand millets (bajra, ragi, jowar) or short-duration pulses (moong, cowpea).
note: Confirm with a local soil test and an agronomist before applying amendments.

issue: Elevated thermal stress during crop cycle
actions: Shift planting windows: advance rabi sowing to avoid terminal heat, or adjust kharif sowing with monsoon onset.
Plant heat-tolerant and early-maturing cultivars recommended by ICAR / State Agricultural Universities.
Apply light protective irrigation during flowering and grain-filling stages to cool down the microclimate canopy.
Maintain tree shelterbelts or agroforestry windbreaks to temper scorching desiccating winds.
note: Confirm with a local soil test and an agronomist before applying amendments.

issue: High interannual rainfall variability or erratic precipitation
actions: Establish contingency cropping plans (alternate early-maturing crops if monsoon onset is delayed by 2-4 weeks).
Practice intercropping (e.g. pigeon pea + soybean, maize + cowpea) to distribute climatic risks.
Enroll in Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) to mitigate localized yield loss risks.
Adopt in-situ moisture conservation: contour bunding, compartmental bunding, and ridge-furrow planting.
note: Confirm with a local soil test and an agronomist before applying amendments.
